moat_against: Near-zero customer switching costs; price capped by Walmart/Amazon/Home Depot/Lowe's
Discretionary big-ticket mix is weather, fuel and farm-income cyclical (Q2 2026 comps -1.5%)
Pet category contested by Chewy, Petco and Walmart
No protection in 2026: guidance cut and long-term framework withdrawn
Store-expansion capex rising into negative comps
moat_for: Dominant rural-lifestyle niche; scale procurement across ~2,400+ Tractor Supply stores plus Petsense
Small-town locations with limited direct farm/ranch competition nearby
Needs-based consumables (feed, pet food) drive repeat trips and retention
Neighbor's Club loyalty base and private brands
Historically high returns on capital through cycles
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow moat (5/10). Tractor Supply is the dominant rural-lifestyle retailer in the US with scale procurement, small-town locations that often face no direct farm/ranch competitor, and a needs-based consumables mix (animal feed, pet food) that drives repeat trips and loyalty. Against that: retail switching costs are near zero, pricing power is capped by Walmart, Amazon, Home Depot and Lowe's, the big-ticket/discretionary half of the mix is weather-, fuel- and farm-income-cyclical (Q2 2026 comps -1.5% on a weak May, drought and fuel costs), and pet faces Chewy/Petco/Walmart. Returns on capital were historically strong but the moat did not prevent a guidance cut and withdrawal of the long-term framework in July 2026. CAP = 8.5 years.
name: Tractor Supply Company
one_liner: Solid niche retailer, moat 5/10, but owner's earnings collapsed on a TTM basis (base $0.46/sh) and it does not clear 15% on any base — weighted IRR 3.9% (TTM) to 7.1% (median base), IV@15% $3.73 vs $33.89 price; clears 15% only below ~$3.73 (TTM base) or ~$11.93 (median base).
